annotations.description: The player has 2 untapped lands and several castable spells but chose to do nothing. Gran-Gran costs {U} and could be cast, providing a body on board and its looting ability when tapped. Artist's Talent costs {1}{R} and could also be cast to enable card filtering. Boomerang Basics could bounce the opponent's Otter token. Firebending Lesson could kill the opponent's 1/1 Otter token. Passing the turn with 2 mana available and multiple playable options wastes tempo in an early game where board development matters. At minimum, Gran-Gran should have been cast as a 1/2 body that generates card selection and enables future cost reduction with Lessons in graveyard.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Gran-Gran for {U}, developing the board with a creature that has relevant abilities (looting when tapped, cost reduction with Lessons in graveyard). Could also consider Artist's Talent for {1}{R} to enable card filtering, or Firebending Lesson to remove opponent's Otter token.

annotations.betterLine: Play Spirebluff Canal as the 2nd land (enters untapped), preserving Island and Riverpyre Verge for later turns when Spirebluff would enter tapped

annotations.description: Duelist of the Mind has flying and vigilance, meaning it can attack for 1 damage through the air with zero downside (stays untapped to block). The opponent has no flyers to block it. This is free damage left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only the Otter Token, leaving Duelist of the Mind back despite having vigilance.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Otter Token and Duelist of the Mind. Duelist has flying (can't be blocked by opponent's Otter) and vigilance (no downside to attacking).

annotations.description: Casting Duelist of the Mind in the precombat main phase is suboptimal. The existing Duelist of the Mind on the battlefield has power equal to cards drawn this turn, and casting spells/creatures before combat doesn't increase its power. More importantly, Frostcliff Siege (choosing Jeskai) would be a stronger play here - it provides card advantage whenever creatures deal combat damage. With a Duelist of the Mind already on board (flying, vigilance), casting Frostcliff Siege before combat would let the Duelist attack and draw a card immediately this turn. The second Duelist of the Mind entering as a 0/3 (having drawn 0 cards this turn) doesn't contribute to combat this turn. Additionally, casting the creature before combat when holding Boomerang Basics (a trick/noncreature spell) means missing the opportunity to sequence optimally - playing Frostcliff Siege would also trigger Artist's Talent-style synergies with the Stormchaser's Talent otter's prowess.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Duelist of the Mind (second copy) in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Frostcliff Siege choosing Jeskai before combat, then attack with the existing Duelist of the Mind and Otter token to trigger the Jeskai draw ability. The second Duelist could be cast post-combat or on a later turn.

annotations.description: Discarded Quantum Riddler instead of Frostcliff Siege, despite reasoning that concluded Frostcliff Siege should be discarded. Quantum Riddler has Warp {1}{U} making it castable cheaply as a 2/2, but Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai mode) provides a consistent card draw engine that synergizes extremely well with two flying Duelist of the Mind on board - each combat damage trigger draws a card, which directly pumps Duelist power. However, the Riddler's Warp ability and late-game potential also have value, making this a close call.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Quantum Riddler
annotations.betterLine: Discard Frostcliff Siege or Boomerang Basics. Keeping Quantum Riddler for Warp {1}{U} as a cheap creature, while Frostcliff Siege competes with other 3-mana plays. Actually, keeping Frostcliff Siege for its synergy with Duelists is likely better.

annotations.description: With 3 mana available (UUG from Steam Vents + 2x Willowrush Verge), casting Stormchaser's Talent for U is fine value, but the sequencing and choice could be debated. The opponent has two Duelist of the Mind on board which are threatening. Boomerang Basics (U) could bounce one of the Duelists, which is a tempo play that also draws a card since it's the opponent's permanent being returned (no, it only draws if you controlled it). Gran-Gran (U) is a 1/2 that loots when tapped AND reduces noncreature spell costs with 3+ Lessons in graveyard - important synergy with the Lesson-heavy hand. However, casting Stormchaser's Talent to get a 1/1 prowess blocker is reasonable given the two Duelists threatening in the air. The main concern is whether Artist's Talent (1R) could have been cast - with UUG available, there's no R source unless Steam Vents taps for R. Steam Vents can tap for U or R, so the player could cast Artist's Talent (1R = using Steam Vents for R + Willowrush for U). Artist's Talent provides looting on noncreature spells which is strong with this hand full of noncreature spells. But Stormchaser's Talent gives a body to block the Duelists and leaves mana open for Firebending Lesson to kill a Duelist. Actually, casting Stormchaser's Talent for U leaves UG open - not enough for Firebending Lesson (R). So this sequencing doesn't enable holding up removal. The play is defensible but there were arguments for other lines.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stormchaser's Talent to create a 1/1 Otter with prowess
annotations.betterLine: Consider casting Gran-Gran (U) first as a blocker that also provides card filtering, or casting Artist's Talent (1R using Steam Vents for R) to set up the looting engine for future turns with a hand full of noncreature spells. Alternatively, holding up Steam Vents for R to cast Firebending Lesson on a Duelist of the Mind (which has 3 toughness, so only 2 damage wouldn't kill it) - though that doesn't work either. Stormchaser's Talent is a reasonable choice.

Bouncing an opponent's Duelist of the Mind with Boomerang Basics while the opponent is completely tapped out would have been a strong tempo play, removing a key threat.

annotations.description: Casting a second Stormchaser's Talent when already having one on the battlefield is low value - the legendary rule doesn't apply to Classes, but the first level ability just creates another 1/1 Otter. Additionally, Artist's Talent at 1R would provide a much stronger value engine (loot on noncreature spells, and can level up for cost reduction). The sequencing is also questionable - they should consider bouncing a Duelist first to stabilize, or casting Artist's Talent for ongoing value rather than getting a second 1/1 token that won't meaningfully help against the opponent's flyers.
